text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to close at $131.83, continuing a sharp pullback from last week's $141 peak. The stock has been pressured by conflicting signals in oil markets: while global crude sits elevated at $130.80 per barrel due to Middle East tensions (Iranian strait closures, Houthi attacks, and airport incidents near Riyadh), U.S. crude is trading at only $107—a gap that limits upside for domestic refiners and producers. The market's initial fear of supply disruptions from Saudi pipeline damage appears to have faded by week's end, removing some of the rally support from earlier in the week.

The broader pressure on energy stocks may also reflect growing economic headwinds: record diesel prices are already straining the transportation sector, and if high energy costs persist, consumer spending and economic growth could weaken—ultimately reducing long-term demand for oil and refined products.
